interest: Shows 1949 plans to move Japan aid to the ECA, using lessons from Clay's Germany while respecting MacArthur.
overview: Labouisse's memo of April 7, 1949 to Webb on moving Japan aid to the ECA, proposing MacArthur as ECA representative with an ECA deputy.

people.name: Henry R. Labouisse, Jr.
people.role: State Department Coordinator for Foreign Aid and Assistance

people.name: Douglas MacArthur
people.role: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers and Commander-in-Chief, U.S. Forces in the Far East

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum evaluating the proposed transfer of administrative responsibility for Japanese rehabilitation and GARIOA funds from the Department of the Army to the Economic Cooperation Administration.
subfiles.summary: Labouisse urges Webb to start talks on moving Japan's GARIOA and rehabilitation programs to the ECA with full control, to avoid Germany's divided authority. He proposes MacArthur as ECA representative with an ECA deputy within SCAP.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Labouisse to Webb on Operation of Japanese Rehabilitation Program by the ECA
